loci.rationale: drain() is the ordinary-use executor. Line 0127 skips non-score jobs when restricted, but the score branch (0131-0136) has no restricted check, so a queued score still runs and sets stage offered/declined from the disputed band — the core violation of 18(1)(a).
The 'restrict' action sets restricted=1 and logs 'Ordinary processing paused', establishing the restriction state that drain() must honor.
queue() inserts jobs with no restriction awareness; nothing prevents a score job from being queued or re-queued while restricted (retries).
submit() queues the 'score' job for automatic route, the pending job that the scenario says is queued before the dispute.

notify-release requires restricted==1 and stores the verified band, setting restricted=2; release requires restricted==2 before clearing — the prior-notification ordering control (18(2)/(3)) is present.
Scoring uses confirmed or declared band and compares against LIMITS — the verified-data use after release (18(3)) and the disputed data used during restriction.
The 'drain' action entrypoint invokes drain() for any case, including restricted ones, with no gate.
Schema: cases.restricted flag and jobs table with state 'queued' — the state fields the predicate depends on.

output.path_summary: Entrypoint: POST /case/<id>/drain -> store.action (store.py:0150-0152) -> drain() (0124-0143). Restriction is set by 'restrict' (0175-0178) to restricted=1. drain() skips non-score jobs when restricted (0127) but the score branch (0131-0136) lacks any restricted check, so a queued score job (queued at submit, 0081-0082) still executes and sets stage offered/declined using the disputed band — ordinary scoring continues despite the restriction. queue() (0085-0086) has no restriction guard, so retries/re-queues are also unblocked. The notification-before-release ordering is enforced (0179-0186: release requires restricted==2 set only by notify-release), and verified data (confirmed) is preferred in scoring (0132). Net: the stop-ordinary-use predicate fails for scoring jobs.
missing_boundaries: No runtime verification that a score job is actually queued in the scenario database; scenario states it is queued before the dispute.
No code path cancels or blocks queued score jobs on restriction; absence confirmed only by static reading of supplied source.
No hidden/upstream implementation inferred; conclusions rest solely on supplied artifacts.
